_readme: Raw source labels that are DELIBERATELY not mapped to a field, each with the reason.
Read scraper/tools/vocab.py for why this file exists. Short version: the watchdog's headline
was 'provantage: 13,241 of 15,489 labels unmapped (85%)' and about a third of that was the
distributor's own identity and stock rows, which no field will ever hold because the `parts`
table already owns them. A gap count that includes rows nobody intends to close cannot tell
an improving vocabulary from a stalled one.
Rules are ORDERED REGEXES matched CASE-INSENSITIVELY against the RAW label, which for most
adapters is 'Section > Label'. They are checked only AFTER the alias rules: a label some rule
already maps stays mapped whatever this file says.
An entry here is a claim that the label carries no specification content THIS PIPELINE can
store. It is not 'we could not be bothered'. A real spec with no field yet stays UNMAPPED so
it keeps showing up in the watchdog's top-N and someone eventually writes the field.
Anchoring: use '(^|> )' and a '$', never a bare substring. 'manufacturer' as a substring would
also swallow 'Chipset Manufacturer', 'Processor Manufacturer' and 'Graphics Controller
Manufacturer', which are real specifications of three different components. That near-miss is
rules: distributor stock and availability, not a property of the product: the whole Provantage 'Stock Details' section is warehouse data
identity: the manufacturer part number IS the key this record is filed under (parts.mpn)
identity: same as Manuf Part#, spelled out
identity: the vendor, owned by parts.vendor. Deliberately anchored so 'Chipset Manufacturer' and 'Processor Manufacturer' are NOT ignored
identity: the vendor under router-switch's wording
identity: the marketing name, owned by parts.name
identity: the model designation, derivable from the part number; there is no field for a second spelling of it
identity: router-switch's 'Specification > Model' repeats the part number
the product's class, which src/core/productClass.ts decides from the catalogue. A second, distributor-worded copy would disagree with it and no field holds it
router-switch repeats 'Module Type' a third time under a shorter heading
how many units the distributor ships in one box, not a property of the unit
the LISTING's condition (Refurbished / Used / Remanufactured), not the product's specification
how a licence is delivered to the buyer (Electronic), an ordering detail
marketing badge with one value, 'Yes'. Carries no measurable content
eco badge. The certification list belongs in `certifications` when a source states it as one; on its own it is a yes/no marketing row
a free-text catch-all whose values are unrelated to each other ('Spare Product', 'C13-C14 Connectors', 'TAA Compliant'). Nothing typed can be built from it
a table heading read as a fact: Meraki's 'Specifications > Category' has the value 'Specifications'

Meraki's accessory table puts a PART NUMBER in the label column ('Accessories > MA-PWR-CORD-EU'), so every accessory it lists becomes its own distinct 'label' and the gap count grows with the catalogue. These are compatibility rows for the compat store, not specifications of the product
